Answer: B
Reason: The initial imaging (Figure 2 and Figure 3) demonstrates a massive left-sided opacity with significant mediastinal shift to the right, indicating a large pleural effusion or tension pathology compressing the left lung. Following the intervention (implied by the question and shown in the resolved state of Figure 4), the mediastinum returns to a central position and the left lung shows significant re-aeration, consistent with successful drainage and resolution of the mass effect.
